Evaluates â€” large-scale empirical repository-mining study of 2,303 agent context files (RQ1 size/readability/structure, RQ2 maintenance, RQ3 instruction content, RQ4 automatic classification with GPT-5); extends the authors' prior study of 253 Claude.md files (PROFES 2025). fields.v: Agent context files, no version: CLAUDE.md (Claude Code), AGENTS.md (OpenAI Codex), copilot-instructions.md (GitHub Copilot)

A single persistent Markdown context file in the repository root, loaded at session start: project-level instructions (system overview, architecture, build/test commands, coding conventions, rules for tools). Observed categories (Table 3, 332 files): Testing 75.9%, Implementation Details 70.8%, Architecture 68.1%, Development Process 65.1%, Build and Run 63.0%, System Overview 59.0%, Maintenance 44.6%, Conf.&Env. 38.9%, Documentation and References 26.8%, Debugging 25.3%, AI Integration 24.1%, DevOps 18.4%, Security 14.8%, Performance 14.5%, UI/UX 8.7%, Project Management 5.4%

File size (words); readability (Flesch Reading Ease); header counts H1-H5; commits per file, inter-commit interval, words added/deleted; manual commit labels (add/fix/del/maintenance); share of files per instruction category; GPT-5 classifier precision/recall/F1 per category; indentation-rule violation rate in AI-authored lines before/after the rule (2 case studies)

Automatic: GitHub API, Textstat (FRE, cross-checked with py-readability-metrics), regex header counts, Lizard, Pydriller, Mann-Whitney U and Cliff's delta. Manual: one inspector labelled readability of 100 files (Spearman 0.19 with FRE); two inspectors labelled 100 commits (34 disagreements, third inspector resolved); grounded-theory coding with LLM-suggested candidate labels (Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5), two inspectors labelled 332 files (2,227 assignments, 80.3% agreement, third inspector resolved, 2,069 final). GPT-5 (temperature 1) classifier compared to human labels

Across agents (not SDD configurations): Claude and Copilot files longer than Codex (small effect, delta 0.21/0.22); Codex files easiest to read (FRE median 51.41 vs Claude 42.39, Copilot 44.39); more H3/H4 for Claude and Copilot; 67.0% of Claude files modified in multiple commits vs 59.8% Copilot, 59.4% Codex; median update interval 23.8 h Claude, 22.3 h Codex, 68.0 h Copilot; Claude places more emphasis on Build and Run (medium effect). Category distributions largely similar across agents

Internal: manual classification bias (two inspectors, 80.3% agreement). Construct: binary presence labels ignore depth; FRE designed for prose, low correlation with human judgment; Markdown header syntax only. External: limited dataset, three agents. Gaps/future work: 'context debt' and context-file smells; ablation of structural elements on agent performance; co-evolution with code and CI linters; NFR blind spot (security, performance) and benchmarks testing NFR adherence; applying the classifier to commit histories

Journal version (TOSEM) of an extension of the authors' PROFES 2025 short paper on 253 Claude.md files (cited as [14]; record rayyan-800485902). Replication package: https://github.com/woraamy/Agent-Context-File-Analysis (data, prompt). Values from text and tables (Table 3, Table 5); Table 3/5 layout jumbled by pdftotext, values rebuilt from text (Table 5 supports sum to 2,069 and match Table 3 percentages over 332 files). Reporting inconsistencies: text says 'half of the files contain system overview' (p. 14) while Table 3 gives 59.0%; 'Maintenance' is called a new category (p. 14) although the earlier study already had it (19.8%); Development Process 65.1% here vs 37.2% in the earlier study. Medians for H2-H5 partly in Fig. 5 only. Indentation case studies are observational, one repository per agent. No pre-registration. Programming language: Not stated (mixed; examples Python, TypeScript, Rust)
fields.why: The earlier study [14] is a PROFES 2025 paper (reference list p. 33), not an MSR-style paper; two reporting inconsistencies were missing (System Overview 'half' vs 59.0%; Maintenance described as new)
